result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A shows all ten signals exactly as supplied in a clean, large-type table, with a short note telling dispatchers to cover the meaning column and quiz themselves. It keeps to direct recall, and its one usage note is brief. B also has the meanings right and adds two-way drills, but it surrounds the list with invented categories, made-up scenarios and a 'mix-up' section, which the rubric marks down. B is also denser and may run past one page. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both sheets give all ten signals with the exact meanings supplied. A is better for self-testing, with a fold-over tip and drills in both directions, but it adds category labels, 'easy to mix up' notes and a drill built on made-up scenarios, which the rubric discourages, and its small, dense type may not fit one page. B is a clean, large-type list for direct recall that clearly fits one page; its self-test is weaker (the 'cover the right column' instruction is ambiguous next to the checkbox column), and its priority note adds a little advice nobody asked for.
